plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Ume trees bloom on bare, dark branches while winter is still in the air. Their small, fragrant flowers open in clouds of white, pink and deep rose. Shrines, parks and old gardens fill with a sweet, spicy scent that people take as the first sign of spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Typically February to March in most of Japan, with some varieties starting earlier
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms have been loved in East Asia for well over a thousand years. In early Japanese poetry they were more admired than cherry blossoms, and ume festivals are still held across Japan each late winter.

plants.name: Prunus dulcis
plants.description: Almond orchards turn hillsides into drifts of snow-white and blush-pink blossom. Each five-petaled flower opens before the leaves, so the whole tree looks wrapped in lace. The effect is especially dreamlike across the rolling Mediterranean countryside.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late January through February in Mallorca
plants.funFact: The almond is a close relative of the peach and plum, and the part we eat is the seed inside a fruit that looks like a small, leathery peach. The trees flower so early that a late frost can ruin a season's crop.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Camellia japonica has glossy evergreen leaves and large, rose-like blooms in crimson, pink and white. The flowers stand out against the dark foliage on cool late-winter days. They are popular garden shrubs in mild coastal climates.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-winter to early spring, with peak bloom in February and March in mild climates
plants.location: Mild coastal regions of the western United States, such as the San Francisco Bay Area
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica belongs to the same genus as the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Breeders have developed thousands of named cultivars of the showy ornamental species.
